body: rain is Acquire and Japan Studio's PlayStation 3 adventure, first released in North America on 1 October 2013. An invisible boy becomes visible only where the rain strikes his body, moving through a city inhabited by creatures governed by the same rule. Shelter changes what can be seen and who can be detected. The player follows the boy through this uncertain landscape, solving problems through the relationship between exposure and concealment. A familiar weather effect becomes the central language of the game, describing both the character's presence and the danger of revealing it.

Beneath an awning or inside a building, the boy disappears from the player and the creatures pursuing him. Wet footprints provide a remaining clue to his position. The player has to use those traces and the surrounding architecture to judge when to move back into the rain. The same rule applies to enemies, so an apparently empty sheltered space may still contain a threat. Progress depends on understanding what the weather reveals and what it conceals, making a small change in cover more important than a conventional new weapon or ability.

Yuki Ikeda directed the game, with Yugo Kanno composing its score. The production uses the limited vocabulary of visibility to organise both puzzles and atmosphere, allowing the setting to explain its dangers through images rather than extensive instructions. European and Japanese releases followed within days of North America. The title's strength comes from the consistency of its central rule. Rain is beautiful because it reveals the child, dangerous because it reveals him to others and useful because its absence can create a safe place, giving one environmental condition several connected meanings.
